title: PostgreSQL
summary: Check relational queries, authorized scope, paging, transactions and data recovery.

sections.label: Documented role
sections.text: The PostgreSQL tutorial introduces relational data and SQL queries.

sections.label: What Atlas provides
sections.text: Selecting PostgreSQL records the technology and version and adds PostgreSQL query, access, transaction and recovery questions to generated skill references. It does not configure a connection or generate a verified query.

sections.label: Check in your environment
sections.text: Confirm the actual version, supported interface, permissions, data model and expected query results. Compare alternatives using your constraints.

sections.label: Review scope
sections.text: The added factual claims use PostgreSQL 18 documentation reviewed on 2026-10-12. The original tutorial reference is retained. Actual project versions, database policies, queries and recovery results require separate evidence.

sections.label: Find the project facts
items: Actual database and driver versions, schema, migration owner, supported application interface and permitted test environment.
Read and write identity, grants, any row security policies, and how the application applies the caller data scope.
Accepted query parameters, expected identifiers, unique ordering, page limits, consistency and freshness requirements.
Transaction and duplicate handling, concurrent updates, migration compatibility, backup and restore evidence. Record only credential sources, never secrets.

sections.label: Documented paging and isolation
sections.text: PostgreSQL 18 recommends a unique ORDER BY for a predictable LIMIT or OFFSET subset. The default Read Committed isolation gives a SELECT its query-start snapshot, and successive SELECT statements can see different committed data, even within one transaction. A stable sort therefore does not establish one snapshot across pages. Choose and test the consistency policy the interface actually provides.

sections.label: Documented transaction and access scope
sections.text: PostgreSQL transactions group steps into an all-or-nothing operation. Row security, when enabled, can restrict the visible or modifiable rows. Superusers and roles with BYPASSRLS bypass it, and table owners normally do too. A successful test with an administrative identity does not establish the behavior of the application identity.

sections.label: Check the data boundary
items: Read the actual schema, approved data interface and migration history. Reuse parameterized operations for values and explicitly permitted query choices.
Check normal, empty and denied reads with the relevant identity. Verify ordering and the agreed consistency while data changes between pages.
Check result identifiers, permitted scope and completeness before preparing any write. Keep write authorization distinct from query validity.
Test the agreed atomic, duplicate and concurrent update behavior. Reconcile an uncertain save before retrying it.
For a schema change, assess old and new application compatibility and the recovery plan. Obtain restoration evidence where required, rather than treating backup existence as proof.
Record actual query or API results, identity, fixtures, database version, cleanup and candidate revision. State which checks remain blocked.

sections.label: Saved selection example
rows: More matching topics than one page
Follow the approved paging contract and save only after the required complete selection is established.
Honor the agreed snapshot or live-result policy. Do not describe stable ordering alone as snapshot consistency.
Stop before persistence and report the save was not authorized.
Use the agreed operation or duplicate contract to establish whether the write occurred before deciding on a retry.

sections.label: Migration and recovery
sections.text: PostgreSQL documents SQL dumps, file system backups and continuous archiving as different backup approaches. The team must choose the applicable method and test its recovery requirements. An application rollback does not automatically reverse a data migration, and a transaction in one database does not undo a remote service call.

sections.label: Useful result
sections.text: A query and persistence contract with expected fixtures for authorized scope, empty data, paging changes, duplicate requests and failed saves. This fictional example proposes a complete permitted selection before saving. Real schema, identifiers, consistency, commands and recovery evidence remain unresolved. No database check or restoration has run.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow use: Architecture and impact, Development, Tests and review. Use when deciding and implementing an affected SQL read or persistence boundary and collecting evidence for its paging, access and transaction behavior. This is an Atlas recommendation reviewed on 2026-10-15, not a mandatory process or an observed execution result.
Check output to obtain: Record the actual schema and driver revisions, application identity, ordering and cross-page consistency contract.
Check output to obtain: Observe permitted, empty and denied results, including a fixture where data changes between pages.
Check output to obtain: Verify the relevant duplicate, concurrent-save and partial-failure outcomes. Keep planned recovery or restoration checks marked unrun until evidence exists.

basis: Scoped documented facts, recommended procedure and illustrative examples
confidence: High for the listed factual claims reviewed on 2026-10-12. Project fit, database access and any query or recovery outcome remain unverified.

catalog.applicability: Use when a PostgreSQL data boundary needs checks for query behavior, permitted scope, paging consistency, transactions or recovery. Selection adds project questions without configuring a connection.
